Adversarial Search and Pruning: author review

Date: 18 October 2026. This edition is an author-reviewed draft, not a student-approved edition.

Teaching and source coverage

The eighteen teaching sections develop state and strategy semantics, backward induction, exact minimax, enforceable guarantees, alpha-beta certificates, an executable implementation, equality and action-selection traps, precise leaf-count assumptions, frontier error bounds, iterative deepening, transpositions, stochastic policies, chance intervals, utility transformations, information constraints, max-n and introductory UCT. The explanation precedes the problem bank.

The bounded comparison covers seven university offerings. Four complementary primary written scopes are Stanford CS221, Berkeley CS188, MIT 6.034 and Cornell CS4700. CMU 15-281 supplies a fifth substantive contribution. Harvard and Yale-hosted AIMA material are comparisons with their authorship and reading boundaries stated. The source audit identifies actual written sections, image-review limits, unavailable material, depth conventions and independently corrected source errors. Prestige and acquisition alone are not treated as scientific validation.

Problems and final decisions

All fifty original or attributed university problems were individually read with their solutions. They include exact backups, complete traces, parameter regions, strict versus nonstrict boundaries, counterexamples, finite counts, error proofs, uncertainty intervals, policy evaluation and UCT calculations. Every solution explains the relevant assumptions, derivation and interpretation. The sixty final rules are complete statements following a coherent summary; they distinguish a conclusion from the hypotheses needed for it.

Two authentic master's questions were reconstructed from inspected original CE booklets: 1403 Question 68 on PDF page 15 and 1404 Question 69 on PDF page 16. Both PDF hashes are checked against the pinned archive manifest. The latter problem includes explicit tests at and on either side of its interval endpoints. Answers are independent derivations, not claims about verified official answer keys. No unverified doctoral item was added merely to fill that category.

Mathematical verification

  • The problem-specific numerical, symbolic-notation and source checks comprise 181 assertions and 533 native MathML expressions.
  • Twenty-seven tree models include 121 independently checked return certificates. A node's working number, exact value and one-sided return flag remain distinct.
  • A separate finite oracle checks 6,651 ordered binary trees and 33,255 narrow-window certificates, ideal-order counts and utility transformations.
  • Crucially, the actual code printed in the lesson was extracted and executed. It passed 6,651 exact-root checks, 6,651 optimal-action checks, 33,255 narrow-window contracts and three consecutive-same-player examples: 46,560 assertions. Thus the code evidence is connected to the printed implementation, not just to a separate purported equivalent.
  • The new native cases environment retains its conventional single left brace and left-aligned alternatives. Existing ordinary, parenthesized and bracketed matrix environments are also checked. Mathematical display expressions remain on one line with local scrolling where necessary.

The text supplies the recursive and algebraic proofs. Finite checks strengthen those arguments; they do not prove literal universal accuracy or a perfect result on every unseen examination.

Diagrams, simulations and browser review

Seventeen compact tree players expose twenty-seven actual-input cases. They show node roles, evaluated leaves, skipped branches, exact versus upper/lower return certificates, legal child order, parameter variations and an explanation at each checkpoint. The separate chance-bound and UCT controls demonstrate their own mathematical mechanisms rather than reusing a generic tree trace.

All 815 rendered tree checkpoints were checked for text padding, canvas containment and attached edge endpoints. Every player passed previous/next/restart/seek controls, and three different players passed actual timed playback and pause. Chance-bound steps and UCT selections were checked against exact or independently computed results. Incoming, currently tightened and original classification windows are explicitly distinguished in both data and displayed labels.

The mobile viewport uses a readable, locally scrollable tree and a complete-tree overview; keyboard and overview navigation were checked, as was automatic centering on the active node. This preserves the compact chapter layout. Source Sans 3, Newsreader, STIX Two Math and JetBrains Mono loaded for prose, headings, mathematics and code respectively. Links and solution controls have no underlines. Three viewport widths, 390, 768 and 1360 pixels, have no document-wide overflow. Print presentation opens all fifty-two solutions and provides final diagrams for all twenty-seven cases, then restores the previous closed state. No runtime errors were observed.

Screenshots and machine-readable evidence are in research/i_games-evidence. These checks cover the current portable Edge implementation and finite interactions. Full PDF pagination and every other browser were not certified.

Edition and delivery boundaries

This is one new technical chapter, counted once after its mathematical and browser gates pass. It does not increase the count of individually revised editions in the original sixty-chapter baseline. Student approval remains unconfirmed. Local files, the self-contained offline copy, GitHub storage and private Site publication are separate delivery records; only verified publication responses establish online availability.
